title: Exam Question Review
objective: Distinguish a necessary condition for series convergence from a sufficient one, and justify the distinction.
questionA: Does the harmonic series ∑ 1/n (from n = 1 to ∞) converge or diverge? Justify your answer.

questionB.stem: A student claims the harmonic series converges because 1/n → 0. Group the terms after the first into blocks ending at 2, 4, 8, ….

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain the flaw in the student’s claim.
parts.credit: 1 point: terms tending to zero is necessary for convergence. 1 point: it is not sufficient; a zero limit alone does not establish convergence.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using the given grouping, explain why each block contributes at least 1/2.
parts.credit: 1 point: block k (k ≥ 1) contains 2^(k−1) terms, ending at index 2^k. 1 point: each term is at least 1/2^k. 1 point: multiplying gives a block sum of at least 1/2. An equivalent general bound earns credit; no credit is required for inventing the grouping.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain what this implies about the partial sums and whether the series converges.
parts.credit: 1 point: the partial sums at block endpoints grow without bound because each added block contributes at least 1/2, so the series diverges.
